description:
Today one guard has three evaluators with three semantics: `eval_dispatch_guard` (src/ir_interp/dispatch_exec.rs: total order, integer-only arithmetic that host-panics on division by zero), `lower_guard_expr` (src/compiler2/jobs/native.rs: unchecked iadd, trapping sdiv, no :badarith), and `emit_dispatch_guard_expr` (src/compiler2/native_codegen/receive.rs: signed integer compare; a float fails to compile, fz-21x.20). A helper in a guard goes through `reify_guard_dispatch`, which re-plans the helper's clauses and inlines them at every call site under a syntactic whitelist (fz-21x.15 lives there; `===` is refused). The planner learns nothing from a guard today (`Region::Guard` is opaque to dispatch_reachability and keying), so changing how a guard runs loses nothing.

Change: each `when` becomes a generated function of its subjects and pins returning boolean, compiled by the ordinary body pipeline (Kernel clauses, typed operators, the inliner), activated in guard mode. In guard mode a callee whose effects fact says `fails` is activated in guard mode too and returns {value, failed}; a `never` call site is failed = true; `arithmetic_result({_, true})` returns failed instead of calling `arithmetic_error`; the guard answers false on any failed lane. Walking `when x + 1 > 0` at the integer maximum: the add reports failure, the guard is false, the next clause answers; the same expression in a body raises :badarith. A callee with fails = false has one activation shared by both modes, so `compare/2` is compiled once. A callee with allocates = true in a guard is a diagnostic.

Callers: `Region::Guard` in entry dispatch, in the receive matcher (through a func ref, hence fz-21x.10 first) and in the interpreter all call the guard function; the projections that hand it subjects stay with the pattern. The guard is its own body, so a guard edit re-lowers one body and the entry and matcher bodies that reference it are reused. The planner keeps `Region::Guard` and `PatternGuardExpr` as planner-only representation (artifact.rs reads it for input demand); the `Dispatch` variant goes.

What goes away: the three evaluators and their helpers (`lower_guard_dispatch`, `lower_guard_dispatch_node`, `lower_guard_binop`, `emit_guard_dispatch`, `emit_short_circuit_guard`, the guard int/float arithmetic in receive.rs, `guard_cmp`, `guard_int`), `reify_guard_dispatch`, `FactKey::GuardDispatch`, `GuardDispatchMap`, `world.guard_dispatch`, `PatternGuardDispatch`, `PatternGuardBindings`, `GuardArgumentId`, `PatternGuardExpr::Dispatch`, the dispatch-pure diagnostics, and fz-21x.15 and fz-21x.20 as defects.

Proof: fixtures guard_arithmetic_failure (Elixir oracle; scratchpad guardfix), guard_overflow (fz's own rule, no oracle), the receive float guard of fz-21x.20, the `===`-in-guard cases restored into cross_kind_operators (scratchpad 8a/8b_guard_identity_cases.txt; Elixir answers :distinct for both), fz-21x.15's repro as a fixture; a heap-counter pin that guard `+` allocates 0 structs; a count pin that `compare/2` has one activation in a program using `<` in both a body and a guard; three doors throughout.
title: Guards are code: one guard function per clause, failure is false, one evaluator on three doors
